title: Factoring a Sum with the GCF

blocks.html: Once you can find the greatest common factor of two numbers, you can write their sum as one product. This is the distributive property used backward, and it is the same move you will soon make with letters.
To factor a sum, pull out the GCF and divide each number by it: $36 + 8 = 4(9 + 2)$, because $36 = 4 \times 9$ and $8 = 4 \times 2$.

blocks.name: areamodel
blocks.cap: A 4 by 9 rectangle and a 4 by 2 rectangle side by side make one 4 by 11 rectangle: $36 + 8 = 4(9 + 2)$.

blocks.html: Picture two rectangles with the same height, 4. One has area 36 (4 by 9), the other has area 8 (4 by 2). Push them together and you get one rectangle 4 tall and $9 + 2$ long. Its area is $4(9 + 2) = 44$, which is $36 + 8$. That is the distributive property: $4(9 + 2) = 4 \times 9 + 4 \times 2$.

blocks.title: Pull out the GCF
blocks.q: Write $24 + 60$ as a product using the GCF.

blocks.html: Pulling out a common factor that is not the greatest. $24 + 60 = 2(12 + 30)$ is true, but 12 and 30 still share a factor of 6, so it is not done. Quick check: the two numbers left inside the parentheses should have no common factor other than 1.
